true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second `downsize` definition overrides the existing 4-argument method

Ruby does not overload class methods by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely replaces the previous `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Existing code that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` will either raise `ArgumentError` (when five arguments are passed) or bind the height integer to `opts`, causing a later `TypeError` in `optimize` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed. Keep one method and explicitly support both call forms or update all callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload size validation is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using site settings

`validateUploadedFile` now sets `maxSizeKB` to `10 * 1024` for every upload type instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 does the same for `max_image_size_kb`. This disables configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` limits in the client: sites with a larger limit reject valid files before upload, and sites with a smaller limit do not warn before the upload is rejected server-side. It is especially wrong for attachments because server-side auto-downsizing only applies to images.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10MB

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a constant. API URL uploads are now capped at 10MB even when the site allows larger files (or has no such small cap), and the setting is ignored for this path. If the intent is to download a larger original before downscaling it, the download cap should be derived from the site setting or a separate explicit setting, not fixed to 10MB.

In-place downsizing can destroy animated GIF originals and ignores conversion failures

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` uses the original upload as both input and output. If `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` picks the non-animated `downsize_instructions`, whose ImageMagick command reads only `#{from}[0]` (the first frame) and writes to `#{to}`. Because `from == to`, a large animated GIF upload is replaced by a static resized first frame and the animation is permanently lost. Also `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` on conversion failure rather than raising, but the return value is ignored; after up to five attempts the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the possibly unchanged, oversized, or partially overwritten file. Downscale to a separate temp file, check the result, and never mutate the original upload path directly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes on nil host

`before_validation` calls `sub!` directly on `self.host`. When `host` is nil or blank, possible via the admin create/update API, `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a normal validation failure. Guard the callback with `self.host.present?` or coerce with `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing record in update/destroy becomes fatal

`update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling nil. A request with a deleted or unknown id passes nil to `save_host` or calls `destroy` on nil, causing a 500 instead of a 404 or JSON error response.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy embeddable hosts are copied without normalization

The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` values verbatim. The old matcher accepted entries with `http://`, `https://`, or trailing paths, while the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the incoming URL's `URI#host` to the stored host string exactly. Existing site settings that contained scheme/path forms will stop matching after migration, breaking embedding for those hosts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator definitions are in the wrong files

`category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category fabricators. Fabrication may load them regardless, but the file names no longer describe their contents and future maintenance by filename will be misleading.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when legacy embed_category is missing or blank

The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` without checking for an empty result. `embed_category` is optional and often blank or unset; in that case the INNER JOIN query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and the migration raises `NoMethodError`, blocking deployment. Use a safe fetch such as `first`/`try` before indexing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
/fruits/:id fixture ignores the requested id

The pretender route always returns `fruits[0]` regardless of `:id`. The updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but still gets fruit 1; the plural `color_ids` assertions happen to pass because fruit 1 also has two colors. This means the test does not actually exercise lookup of a different record and could mask regressions.

Host entries with ports cannot match

The format validation allows a port such as `example.com:8080`, but `record_for_host` compares `URI(host).host`, which drops the port, against the stored host string. A stored host with a port can never match an incoming referer, so such entries appear valid in admin but silently deny embeds. Either strip ports on save and adjust lookup, or disallow them.

No uniqueness constraint on host

There is no unique validation or index on `host`. The admin API/UI can create multiple `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host with different categories, while `record_for_host` returns the first one. Imported topics then use whichever row is returned first, making the host-to-category mapping ambiguous and nondeterministic.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicUser.find_by(...) can return nil for a logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL without having a TopicUser row for that topic, for example by visiting /t/.../unsubscribe directly for a topic they never interacted with. The next line calls tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError and a 500. Use TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by, TopicUser.change, or handle nil explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
No assertion for the new topic unsubscribe URL or controller behavior

The spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the MessageBuilder input but still only asserts the existing user_preferences_url appears in the body. It does not check that the topic-specific unsubscribe URL appears in the text or HTML, and there are no specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe or Topic#unsubscribe_url, leaving the new behavior effectively untested.

State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed via GET without CSRF protection

The new route maps GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe to a controller action that mutates TopicUser.notification_level based only on the current session. Because there is no CSRF token or per-message secret, any website visited by a logged-in user can embed an image or request to that URL and silently change their notification level for a topic.

unsubscribe_link interpolation now requires unsubscribe_url from every caller

The shared unsubscribe_link translation now contains %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder interpolates it whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Only send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url. Any other MessageBuilder call with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the text or HTML body, breaking those emails. Either provide a default value in MessageBuilder or update all callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
match_count updates are non-atomic and double-count signup attempts

`match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write and can lose increments under concurrent attempts. Additionally, UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, both of which run validations; since EmailValidator invokes `should_block?` during validation, a single signup attempt with a matching BlockedEmail increments match_count twice. This makes the match statistics unreliable and adds extra database writes during validation. Use an atomic counter update and/or avoid running the validator twice for the same attempt.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email matching is case-sensitive and bypassable

`should_block?` compares the raw email value against `blocked_emails.email` with no normalization, and the User signup path shown in this diff does not downcase email before validation. Email address routing is case-insensitive, so a mixed-case address such as `Bad@example.com` will not match a blocked record stored as `bad@example.com`. An attacker can bypass the block by changing case. Normalize with `Email.downcase` both when creating BlockedEmail records and before querying/validating.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Server-side EmailValidator does not validate email syntax

validate_each only checks domain whitelist/blacklist and BlockedEmail. It never verifies that value is a syntactically valid email address. Because this is the validator wired through `validates :email, email: true` in User, a direct POST to /users with a malformed non-blank email (for example `foo` or `a@`) can pass validation if client-side checks are bypassed, resulting in a user record with an invalid email. Add a server-side email format check.

change_email does not enforce the blocked email list

The change_email path only checks whether another user already has the requested email and then creates an email token. It never calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` or otherwise runs the email validator, so an existing user can request a change to a blocked address. This sends a confirmation email to the blocked address and, depending on EmailToken confirmation behavior, may complete the change. The blocked-email control should be applied here before the email token is created.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL instead of origin

`request.referer` is the full embedding page URL (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/...`), but `Window.postMessage` requires the target origin (`http://eviltrout.com`). Passing the full URL with a path prevents the resize message from being delivered to the parent page, so the iframe height is never updated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized

`url` is interpolated directly into HTML without escaping and only checked to start with `http(s)://`, so a URL like `http://evil.com/'><script>...` is injectable. The resulting `contents` are stored via PostCreator with `cook_method: raw_html` and then rendered in `embed/best` with `raw post.cooked`, so attacker-controlled feed or imported HTML can execute script in the forum embed context.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB syntax breaks embed rendering

The tag `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby/ERB; `end` cannot be followed by a postfix `if` like this. Template compilation raises a SyntaxError whenever this view is rendered, so the embed page will fail once a topic exists.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed crashes on RSS items without content

`i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` member. Many valid feeds only provide `description` or `summary`, so `i.content` is nil and the job raises, and since retry is disabled the entire poll run fails. The parser should use `i.content || i.description || i.summary` or explicitly skip missing content.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Missing embed_by_username causes nil.downcase crash

`fetch_http` calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking the setting is present. If an embed is requested while `embeddable_host` is set but `embed_by_username` is not configured, the background job raises NoMethodError, so the loading page never resolves. This is an easy misconfiguration and should return or fallback instead of crashing.

Throttle key expiration is not atomic with creation

`retrieved_recently?` calls `$redis.setnx` and then `$redis.expire` separately. If the process crashes between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is left without a TTL and the URL is effectively throttled forever. This should be done with an atomic `SET NX EX`-style command or ensure expiration in a Redis transaction.

iframe URL is malformed when discourseUrl has no trailing slash

`discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` concatenates the path without a separator. If `discourseUrl` is configured as `http://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), the iframe src becomes `http://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which fails to load. Use `discourseUrl + "/embed/best?..."` or normalize the base URL.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Small-action button no longer right-aligned after flexbox conversion

The `.small-action` container is now a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, but the existing `button` rule still has `float: right` (line 309). Floats are ignored on flex items, and there is no `margin-left: auto` on the button or `flex-grow` on `.small-action-desc` to push it to the right edge. As a result, the button is laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` rather than at the right edge of the row.

align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align for old Firefox fallback

`flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box`, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding old Firefox property `-moz-box-align`. In a Firefox build that relies on the `-moz-box` fallback, the `center` or `baseline` alignment will be ignored. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` or remove the `-moz-box` display fallbacks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`include_website_name` is misnamed and dead code

Serializer inclusion callbacks use `include_website_name?` with a trailing question mark, and `untrusted_attributes` already defines that callback for `:website_name`. Defining `include_website_name` without `?` has no effect. It should be removed; simply renaming it to `include_website_name?` would override the untrusted guard and could expose `website_name` to restricted anonymous TL0 users.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check misses website subdomains such as www.example.com

The `else` branch only treats the user's website domain as a parent/suffix of the Discourse host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`). It does not handle the reverse case where the website is a subdomain of the Discourse host. For example, with `Discourse.current_hostname == 'example.com'` and `website == 'http://www.example.com/user'`, `website_name` returns `'www.example.com'` and drops `/user`, even though the sibling-subdomain logic indicates subdomains of the same registrable domain should show the path. This makes the new UX fail for the common bare-apex vs `www` configuration.

TL0 anonymous untrusted attribute list not updated

`website_name` was added to the serializer's `untrusted_attributes` list, but the local `untrusted_attributes` array in the TL0 anonymous test still omits `:website_name`. The current test would pass even if `website_name` were exposed because no `website` is set in that context. Add a profile website and assert that `json` does not have `:website_name`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

Embedded post author link light-theme color changed from 30% to 70%

Missed dark-theme conversion for category badge notification color

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages off by one for exact multiples of limit

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 with the default limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. As a result showingLast is false, the next control is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count, loading an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), preserving the existing zero-member special case.

true_positives.golden_comment: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Automatic remove_member test uses PUT instead of DELETE

The route for remove_member is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" and the client sends DELETE. This spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member. Because controller specs dispatch the given action directly, the test does not verify that the production HTTP verb is routable and could pass even if the DELETE route is broken or removed. It should use xhr :delete, :remove_member.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 with the default limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Automatic group check evaluates against member user instead of group

group_member.hbs is used as the itemView for each member in {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so the template context is the member User object, not the group. User has no automatic property, so automatic is undefined/falsy and {{#unless automatic}} renders the remove link even for automatic groups. The server rejects removal with 422, but the UI exposes a control that fails with no client-side error handling.

PATCH update semantics were removed but PATCH still routes to update

The old update distinguished request.patch? and processed params[:changes] for incremental membership changes. The new update ignores changes, so a PATCH request (which resources :groups still routes to this action) will not add or remove members. Worse, because params[:visible] is absent, group.visible is set to false. Existing PATCH clients can silently hide a group and receive a success response.

Public members endpoint response shape changed from array to object

Previously /groups/:group_id/members returned a JSON array of serialized users. It now returns an object with members and meta. Existing consumers of this public route that expect a top-level array will break. The SPA client was updated, but this is an unversioned contract change to a public API path.
